pr_body:
The `--run_under 'cd $DIR && '` trick didn't work, so instead we inject
the path to the workspace via an environment variable and set the
sandbox writable paths accordingly.

Also update `pkg/spanconfig/spanconfigstore` test to use the
Bazel-friendly utils for finding `testdata`.

Closes #69570.

Release note: None

issue_context.title: bazel: support `--rewrite` for datadriven and logic tests
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

We have various datadriven and logic tests in CRDB that make use of golden datafiles, and support a `--rewrite` flag to update those golden files. Without --rewrite these datafiles are opened in [read-only mode](https://github.com/cockroachdb/datadriven/blob/e89bf9ee1861a9bf55863a1d50a3672a1ceefb18/datadriven.go#L116), so works fine. With `--rewrite` we use the [read-write mode](https://github.com/cockroachdb/datadriven/blob/e89bf9ee1861a9bf55863a1d50a3672a1ceefb18/datadriven.go#L120), which is not permitted over [data dependencies in the sandbox](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/7057d2fe785535aceaf1db0c418632e305d79dc7/pkg/sql/opt/exec/execbuilder/BUILD.bazel#L57).

Strawman: we could instruct the libraries to write to another path (when run under bazel) and copy those files over those files into source tree. Bazel supports a [`TEST_UNDECLARED_OUTPUTS_DIR`](https://docs.bazel.build/versions/main/test-encyclopedia.html#initial-conditions) envvar that could work as a test-specific scratch space. It doesn't have to be `dev` copying over these files smartly, the tests could do it themselves by checking `bazel.BuiltWithBazel()` provided we include the various testdata directories as part of our `--sandbox_writable_path`. Datadriven for e.g. takes in the path it [reads/writes from](https://github.com/cockroachdb/datadriven/blob/master/datadriven.go#L114); a hacky prototype in some other project:

```go
func cp(t *testing.T, src, dest string) {
	input, err := ioutil.ReadFile(src)
	require.Nil(t, err)
	require.Nil(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dest), 0755))
	if err := ioutil.WriteFile(dest, input, 0644); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	require.Nil(t, ioutil.WriteFile(dest, input, 0644))
}

func TestDatadriven(t *testing.T) {
	outdir := os.Getenv("TEST_UNDECLARED_OUTPUTS_DIR")
	workspace := os.Getenv("BAZEL_WORKSPACE") // passed in using --test_env=BAZEL_WORKSPACE=<...>, is there a better way?
	datadriven.Walk(t, "testdata", func(t *testing.T, path string) {
		dest := filepath.Join(outdir, path)
		cp(t, path, dest)
		defer func() { cp(t, dest, filepath.Join(repo, "<package name>", path)) }()

		datadriven.RunTest(t, dest, func(t *testing.T, d *datadriven.TestData) string {

```


**To Reproduce**

```sh
$ dev test pkg/sql/opt/exec/execbuilder -f=TestExecBuild/local/delete # read-only mode; passes
$ bazel test --config=devdarwinx86_64 //pkg/sql/opt/exec/execbuilder:execbuilder_test \  # read-write mode; fails
    --test_filter=TestExecBuild/local/delete --test_output errors --test_arg -rewrite
...
--- FAIL: TestExecBuild (0.29s)
    test_log_scope.go:73: test logs captured to: /var/folders/3j/6fxg9ckn21g5xm0z_06r7gzr0000gn/T/logTestExecBuild048473035
    test_log_scope.go:74: use -show-logs to present logs inline
    --- FAIL: TestExecBuild/local (0.23s)
        --- FAIL: TestExecBuild/local/delete (0.23s)
            logic.go:3127:
                testdata/delete:247: error while processing
            logic.go:3127: open testdata/delete: operation not permitted
    logic.go:3359: -- test log scope end --
FAIL
```

**Expected behavior**

The test to pass.

Epic CRDB-8036
comments: Seems like a fool's errand to make this work with `bazel test`, but I imagine it would be fairly easy to make this work with `bazel run`. (Still might require some changes on the Go side of course.) `bazel run` doesn't have the same rules with the `--sandbox_writable_path` stuff.

review_comments: Let's file an issue/tracking somewhere about all the other callsites that need to be updated in this same way. Probably we want a linter for it, but going through our datadriven tests and updating each one seems worth doing as well.
I'm not really sure what additional flags get passed down to rewrite, examples? Something worth adding tests for? It doesn't map to anything in our makefile either, so I'd be ok with removing it.

See https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C019A8NANH0/p1632782526029000 for previous discussion

Quote Andrew Warner: 

> For example, a bunch of tests have --rewrite flags to tell the test to rewrite their expectations. Sometimes these --rewrite flags take patterns to tell it what to rewrite.
(Also, I think this is redundant with us using NoOptDefVal above.)
No, this ensures that `rewrite` gets set to a value if `--rewrite-arg` is set but `--rewrite` isn't passed.

I feel the boolean switch form was easier to use, what other arguments are we expecting to use here? Wouldn't callers have to additionally specify `-rewrite` (`dev test ... --rewrite -rewrite`) as well? Not sure how it plays with the -rewrite-arg below.

The `NoOptDefVal` below ensures that the default value of the `--rewrite` flag if passed without an option is `-rewrite`. So `dev test ... --rewrite` works exactly as before. If the `rewrite` you need to pass down to the test binary requires two `-`'s you instead need `--rewrite=--rewrite`. 🤷
AFAIK we haven't standardized across one spelling (either `--rewrite` or `-rewrite`) in the codebase. If and when we do, then this can be collapsed back to a bool.

We're not using --run_under anymore, I think this can go away.

EDIT: Actually, doesn't look like it works. That said, it makes sense to disallow stress + rewrite; worth updating the comment to remove the --run_under reference.
Worth adding a test case for using multiple test targets with `--rewrite`, now that it's supported.
